newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA SAYS MONETARY, FISCAL POLICIES TIGHTENED.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA SAYS MONETARY, FISCAL POLICIES TIGHTENED.

text.p: Indonesian Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Thursday that tight monetary and fiscal policies were in place and that their continuation would depend on developments.
"We are tightening monetary and fiscal policy," he told reporters after speaking at a capital markets conference.
"The amount will depend on developments," he said without elaborating.
"Yesterday you know that our central bank raised interest rates," Mar'ie added. "It is a signal that we are still tightening our policy."

The minister did not refer specifically to Bank Indonesia's decision on Thursday to scrap the announcement of its intervention and conversion bands, seen by the market as a managed float of the rupiah.
The bank had raised interest rates of its certificates of all maturities by 100 basis points on Wednesday in a vain bid to stem a slide in the rupiah.
On Thursday, the rupiah plunged more than 100 points after the central bank announcement and was trading at a historic low of 2,750/800 against the dollar at 0425 GMT.
